params.body:
Guilherme's weekly posts arrive as PDFs and were typed into the Studio by hand; the previous batch of fifty-eight came in that way. Their text is already in the shape the Studio knows (one json per post, made from the PDFs by a converter that lives beside them), so retyping it adds nothing but a chance of drift from what the author wrote.

`node bin/import-articles.mjs <folder> [--dry] [--update] [--tier=free]` reads that folder and writes the pieces through the articles store.

**Three rules, all about who decides.**

- **Everything lands as `draft`.** The tags are machine-guessed, the elements are missing and no evidence is attached yet. An import that publishes puts pieces on gentells.com that nobody has read; editorial moves them on in the Studio.
- **What is already there stays.** Matched on title (the id in the json derives from the title, so a second run would otherwise double every post). A person may have touched it since: a tag corrected, evidence attached, the dek rewritten. `--update` does overwrite, but only the fields from the json and only on a piece that is still a draft.
- **Nothing is invented.** No title, or a body under 400 characters, and the piece is skipped with a reason. Half a post in the database is worse than none: in the Studio it looks like finished work.

`test/import-articles.test.mjs` pins those three. Full suite: 697 pass.

Tried against the 68 posts in `posts-pdf`: 68 drafts on the first run, 0 created and 68 skipped on the second.
params.title: Guilherme's posts come in as drafts, not as published work
